title: Bring your client into the passkey ecosystem
description: Help people use their existing Nostr identity in your app. Request a compatibility review and agree a safe integration path.
ctaNote: Opens a public GitHub form in a new tab. A GitHub account is required.
status: Integration support is under review. A request does not grant access or guarantee compatibility.
pathsTitle: Choose the access your app needs
signerBody: Request signing operations while identity keys remain in the user’s signer. Use a supported signer protocol when your app does not need the keys.
recoveryBody: Your client receives key material and may open a whole vault. This needs explicit consent, compatible recovery formats and source-owner approval for cross-origin access.
project: Your project, public code or documentation, and a maintainer contact.
origins: Exact production and staging origins, the source RP domain, and the direction of access.
scope: The user journey, which secrets your client sees, what it stores, and how logout and recovery work.
evidence: Implementation versions, supported browsers/devices, disposable-account test results and a pilot plan. Mark untested cases.
step1Body: Describe your integration in the GitHub form. Keep confidential information out of the public issue.
step2Body: Maintainers review formats, secret scope and exact origins with you. Both the source and receiving client have work to do.
step3Body: Verify recovery on supported devices, agree a limited pilot and record compatible versions before enabling access.
limitsTitle: A supported source is more than a name
limitsBody: Each passkey request targets one RP domain. Listing a source does not authorize it. Browser support, source permission and recovery compatibility must all be verified; native app associations are separate.
privacyBody: Never post seeds, private keys, PRF outputs, tokens, credential IDs or personal vaults. Use private security reporting for vulnerabilities or sensitive security details.
cardBody: Build a compatible client and request an interoperability review.
